narration.text: ResilientMesh — guided demonstration
Everything below runs on this machine. No Docker, no account, no
payment credentials, and no network once the module cache is warm.
Scenario   issuer-outage, seed 42, 10 failures/sec
Inference  LIVE — openai/gpt-oss-120b
falling back to cassette replay, then the deterministic classifier
Time       waits compressed 240x so retries land while you watch;
decisions unchanged, regulatory delays never compressed
0. Booting the real system
· Starting embedded PostgreSQL 18.3 and an in-process Redis server
· Initialising an empty database, so this run depends on nothing before it
[ok] Up in 38.0s — API on 127.0.0.1:8080, Razorpay API on 127.0.0.1:8081
Open these now if you want to watch it live:
Ops console   http://127.0.0.1:8080/console.html
Checkout      http://127.0.0.1:8080/checkout.html
Ops token     [redacted]
The token is generated per run and exists nowhere else. The console is
read-only; every mutating action lives in meshctl, behind --yes.
1. A bank goes down and failed payments start arriving
The simulator serves Razorpay's real schemas and signs real HMAC
webhooks. The edge verifies the signature before it parses anything.
[ok] 8 incidents recorded
PAYMENT             ISSUER           DECLINE                  AMOUNT          STATE
pay_XD0nBPG9aT3YHf  netbanking:SBIN  authentication_failed    ₹6,829.00     SCHEDULED
pay_8vPeV6R3qehsGN  netbanking:HDFC  payment_failed           ₹2,249.00     SCHEDULED
pay_8GFsLzJwJTgUIN  netbanking:ICIC  insufficient_funds       ₹4,811.00     EXECUTING
pay_nLuP6TRLhYUFTx  netbanking:HDFC  bank_technical_error     ₹3,494.00     SCHEDULED
pay_sqaWXIFDrPCpH8  netbanking:ICIC  payment_failed           ₹4,685.00     EXECUTING
pay_5gEZgywU7HNWCv  upi:oksbi        upi_collect_expired      ₹199.00       SCHEDULED
pay_z6esELKYiwjzK2  card:ICIC        invalid_otp              ₹939.00       EXECUTING
pay_bDEHVc295COswR  card:ICIC        gateway_technical_error  ₹1,52,574.00  SCHEDULED
Real Razorpay decline codes against real Indian issuer codes. Amounts
are integer paisa end to end; no float touches a money path.
2. What the model proposes, and what the gatekeeper allows
The model is advisory. It receives a bucketed, allowlisted context
with no PII, and returns a proposal that has no amount field at all —
not a validated one, no field — so it cannot propose a different sum.
[ok] 8 gate decisions
One incident, end to end:
pay_bDEHVc295COswR  ₹1,52,574.00 via card  card:ICIC
declined "gateway_technical_error"
WEBHOOK_ACCEPTED       gateway_technical_error, ₹1,52,574.00, signature verified
DIAGNOSIS_PROPOSED     HEURISTIC proposed ASYNC_EXPONENTIAL_RETRY at 0.60 — upstream infrastructure fault at card:ICIC with no declin…
GATE_DECISION          ASYNC_EXPONENTIAL_RETRY on card after 60s  [AMOUNT_PINNED DELAY_BOUNDS]
INCIDENT_SCHEDULED     deferred 60s; the due time is written to the incident row
Decided by LIVE 1   HEURISTIC 7
Every decision names the tier that made it. A model returning
{"mode":"LIVE"} cannot promote its own answer: those fields carry
json:"-".
3. The decisions it refuses to make
This is the half that matters. A recovery system that only logs its
successes cannot be audited, so every abstention is recorded with the
invariant that caused it.
[ok] 6 distinct invariants have refused something
INVARIANT             TIMES FIRED  WHAT IT PREVENTS
TERMINAL_DECLINE      3            a decline no retry can fix, so no fee is spent
AMOUNT_PINNED         1            the amount can only come from the signed payload
DELAY_BOUNDS          1            the schedule stays inside a sane horizon
RBI_AFA_CEILING       1            above the ceiling a debit needs authentication
RBI_MANDATE_COOLING   1            RBI's 24-hour gap between recurring debits
RBI_PRE_DEBIT_NOTICE  1            the payer must be warned before a debit
All 14 invariants are deterministic and proved exhaustively over 510,720
reachable states. `go run ./cmd/modelcheck` re-derives that.
4. Payments recovering
A deferred retry writes an absolute due time to its own row, so it
survives a restart. A sweeper claims due rows and re-publishes them.
[ok] 10 recovered, 5 scheduled, 1 abstained
· Letting the outage run for a further 1m15s before reading the outcome
[ok] Soak complete: 39 recovered, 18 scheduled, 4 abstained
OUTCOME    COUNT
RECOVERED  39
SCHEDULED  18
ABSTAINED  4
EXECUTING  35
Recovered  ₹5,33,478.00 of merchant revenue
Cost       ₹117.50 in gateway fees to do it
Both read from the attempts table, not from a counter. The table has a
unique constraint on (incident, attempt number), so a retried write
cannot double-count a fee — a defect deterministic simulation found.
5. The audit ledger, and an attack on it
Every consequential decision is hash-chained, with each field absorbed
length-prefixed so an attacker controlling two adjacent fields cannot
forge a collision by shifting the boundary between them.
[ok] Chain intact: 594 entries verified, head 11c9974b470f1bb4…
[ok] Evidence pack for pay_065x7ransd2P…: 9 entries provable in 14.6 kB against a 594-entry ledger
Each entry carries an inclusion proof of about ten sibling hashes rather
than the ledger it came from, so the bundle proves this payment and
discloses nothing about any other.
· Editing entry 297 directly in PostgreSQL, as an attacker with database access would
[ok] Detected at entry 297 — the exact row that was edited
Cause: hash mismatch
The row edited is in the middle of the chain, not the head. A ledger
that only catches a modified head catches nothing, because the head is
what an attacker rewrites last.
Done
Elapsed    142 seconds
What this run proved, in order:
1. The system boots on a clean machine with no dependencies to install.
2. Signed webhooks are verified before anything parses them.
3. Every decision names the tier that made it and the rules applied.
4. Refusals are recorded as carefully as actions.
5. Deferred retries survive and complete, and money is recovered.
6. The audit ledger detects tampering at the exact row.
Verify any of it independently:
go run ./cmd/meshctl selftest      the same loop, as a pass/fail gate
go run ./cmd/modelcheck            510,720 states, 9 invariants, 0 violations
go test ./... -count=1             the full suite
./scripts/judge.sh                 every gate, with a written report
